posts.text: Go build plugins for Claude! https://claude.com/docs/build/overview

Plugins are the main way for third-party developers to create extensions for Claude. Over the coming weeks, one discovery experience will roll out across Claude and Claude Code. Read the blog to learn more: https://claude.com/blog/build-plugins-for-claude

It’s now easier to build plugins for Claude. We built a new portal to submit your plugin, track review, and see usage. Plugins package MCP and skills, and are becoming the way to build for Claude. MCP usage across Claude products is up 110x this year! https://claude.com/blog/build-plugins-for-claude

As we roll this out, it's available for: - Pro plans once a week - Max and Team Premium plans each time a 5-hour session limit is hit. If you need to keep going past the wrap-up, you can continue with extra usage.

Claude Code will now try to find a graceful stopping point when you hit your 5-hour limit mid-task, instead of cutting off mid-edit. It gets a small, fixed allowance pulled from your weekly limit to wrap up what it can.

Opus 5.5 is 20% cheaper per input and output token than Opus 5, and 60% cheaper on cache reads. So what does that actually do to the cost of a task in Claude Code? We ran the numbers, and built a calculator so you can run yours from /usage: https://claude.dev/blog/what-a-task-costs-on-opus-5-5/

Today, we'll resume charging for requests our safeguards block before Claude responds. This only applies in categories with low false positive rates: biology, distillation attacks, and frontier LLM development. We've seen some coordinated attacks on our systems in recent weeks, and this is one layer of defense. In recent testing, 99.7% of accounts using Claude Code, Claude​.ai, or Cowork did not hit any of these newly "billable blocks." The classifiers behind the blocks we’re resuming charging for today are tuned to have a <0.1% false positive rate. We know that's not 0%, and we're going to keep improving them so they interrupt your work less often. If you think a request has been blocked incorrectly, please report it with /feedback in Claude Code. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback#how-refusals-are-billed

Sorry for any confusion! Cloud sessions run on your Pro or Max plan, like the rest of Claude Code. This promo is an optional one-time credit that your cloud sessions spend first, before falling back onto your normal plan usage. We hope you enjoy the credits!
We've just added local support to Projects in Claude Code, so threads can now run on your own machine.

We're working through the waitlist, and are giving access to Projects to more Pro and Max users. If you used Claude projects before, we're still working on migrating you over. The early access waitlist if you haven't signed up yet: https://claude.com/form/projects

The credit is separate from your usage limits, and it applies automatically once you start a cloud session. If you hit a limit locally, keep going in the cloud until your credit runs out. One credit per account, for cloud sessions only.
Follow the link below to claim the credit or run /claim-credit in the CLI. You’ll need GitHub connected to start a session. Claim by Oct 7. Terms apply. https://claude.ai/code/claim-credit/10

Cloud sessions are officially available and out of research preview! They let you keep Claude Code working, even when your laptop is closed. Existing subscribers get a one-time credit to try them: $100 on Pro, $250 on Max.
Browse the marketplace: https://claude.com/marketplace And if you're building for Claude, list your tools, agents or services here: https://claude.com/blog/claude-marketplace

You can now discover tools, agents and expert partners on Claude Marketplace. Use it to: - Add connectors and plugins like Slack and Notion - Buy agents and products from companies like Cursor and CrowdStrike - Scale with service partners like Accenture and Deloitte
We made claude​.ai 3x faster in two weeks. Here’s how we use Claude to measure, debug and improve performance. Prompts and methods included. https://claude.dev/blog/how-we-made-claude-ai-faster/

Try these in your first Opus 5.5 session: → Hand over a whole task. Define "done" and when to check in. → Drop "think carefully". It always thinks first. → After a long run, check what it needs to go further. Our playbook: https://claude.dev/blog/getting-the-most-out-of-opus-5-5/
An algorithmic drawing program created by @kevin_t_ngo. Every drawing is based on a different seed.
Claude Opus 5.5 is available today. What will you explore?
A thread of early explorations with Claude Opus 5.5: A short story about a watermelon created by @kevin_t_ngo.
Opus 5.5 is available now in Claude Code and the Claude Platform. With its intelligence, lower price, and speed, it's our new daily driver for coding and agentic work. We hope it'll become yours too.

As our models grow more powerful, safeguards are one way we prevent misuse. Opus 5.5 is the first Opus with Fable 5.1-class safeguards on cyber, bio, and frontier LLM development. Flagged requests fall back to another model, and we're working to reduce incorrect flags.

Opus 5.5 performs at the level of Fable 5.1. It's ~30% faster and ~40% cheaper than Opus 5 per task. In Claude Code: - 5-hour session limits increase 20% today - Opus 5.5 is priced lower, so it goes 25% further within limits - Pro, Max, and Team users get a reset to use anytime

A Philip Marlowe radio drama is a classic hard-boiled detective series based on Raymond Chandler’s private eye. The main one, The Adventures of Philip Marlowe (NBC 1947, CBS 1948-51), starred Van Heflin then Gerald Mohr. It sounds like pure audio noir: Mohr’s rich baritone delivering cynical, world-weary narration packed with sharp similes, tense dialogue, rain-slick streets, footsteps, phones, gunshots, and dramatic music cues. Gritty, atmospheric, and driven by imagination.
